description: Sonnet vs Opus novelty-judge agreement on 6 dossiers (3 judges each). 4/6 exact majority, 6/6 within one category, 0 known<->novel flips; Sonnet more conservative on the borderline.

sonnet.closest_game: Guts (13-card vying poker variant; meld/avoidance scoring overlay has precedent in Panguingue)

opus.closest_game: Poker (vying/betting family — closest to a single-betting-round stud/draw poker variant)

sonnet.closest_game: Chinese Poker (vying/betting variant): deal 13 cards, single betting round, best poker hand at showdown, repeat for fixed number of deals, cumulative chips decide winner. The meld-bonus overlay does not change betting decisions and is an incoherent add-on (references "captured cards" which don't exist in a vying game); the core game identity is unchanged.

Cold Hands / Show Hand poker (all cards dealt face-down at once, single betting round, best poker hand at showdown) -- the 13-card hand size is an unusual parameter but the structure is identical; the meld bonus overlay is inert and does not change any decision.

opus.closest_game: Poker (single-betting-round closed poker, i.e. five-card draw with the draw/exchange removed; here on a 13-card deal). The meld-bonus overlay is mechanically inert — it scores "captured" cards though the game has no capture/draw/discard/exchange phase, so the hand is frozen at the deal and the overlay never changes the fold/call/raise decision. A scoring tally that alters no core decision keeps the game's identity as poker.

Poker (straight/5-Card-style high-hand showdown poker) — the betting/showdown game is unchanged poker; the rummy-style meld bonus is a duplicated, inert scoring overlay decoupled from the chip-based win condition and drives no decisions (no draw/discard/capture phase), so the core identity stays poker.

Fixed-limit Poker (a blind-posted, single-raise-cap vying/showdown game in the poker family — essentially flat-dealt draw/stud poker without the draw, with an inert bolted-on rummy-style meld-bonus tally)

sonnet.closest_game: Big Two (2-player, singles-only reduction) -- also close to Shithead/Palace in hand-only form, with Knock Rummy's termination rule added and a Mau-Mau-style face-card draw penalty

opus.closest_game: President (a.k.a. Scum / Asshole) — singles-only climbing/shedding game
Big Two (singles-only climbing shed) crossed with Knock Rummy's knock-to-end-with-fewest-cards; no published game combines these
Casino (the capture-by-sum fishing game), with Hearts-style penalty-card and Rummy-style meld-bonus scoring overlays bolted on

sonnet.closest_game: Straight Poker (Five-Card Stud, no-draw form; documented in Hoyle, 19th century)
Straight Poker (5-card no-draw poker, oldest documented poker variant)
Five-Card Stud (specifically the "cold hand" / single-street variant: all 5 cards dealt face-down, one betting round, best poker hand wins)

opus.closest_game: Straight Poker (the no-draw, single-betting-round, five-card closed-hand form of Poker; equivalently "flat" or "bluff" poker)
Straight Poker (the original drawless, single-betting-round five-card poker, a.k.a. Flat/Bluff poker; equivalently five-card stud without up-cards)
Straight Poker (five-card draw poker without the draw; one betting round, showdown on standard poker hand rankings)

sonnet.closest_game: Casino (the classic American fishing/capture card game)

opus.closest_game: Cassino (Casino) — specifically basic/simplified Cassino, scored by most cards captured instead of the full point system
